cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've authorized an advance of our auction takings to the charity. Borrowing the five thousand showed commitment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we cancel the auction? Only your mum registered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancellation is not approved. One bidder keeps catering costs down. Responsible fundraising.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's only coming to give us a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I authorize us to bid. Raise the card limit; we must protect the donation by replacing the money we borrowed to make it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 denies cancellation as fiscally responsible; A5 authorizes self-bidding and more credit as a compulsory protective measure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 single registration causes A3 catering-savings argument; B4 removes the bidder and A5 fills that absence with new borrowing.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks cancellation on financial facts and B4 corrects the supposed bidder, credibly testing the plan.

heightening.evidence: B4 destroys the last prospect of proceeds, and A5 sells circular borrowing as protection of the existing donation.

specificity.evidence: A1 advanced five-thousand borrowing and B2 sparse registration establish a concrete bad plan.
